races.name: Alex And Salvo Welcome You To The Bridge Handicap
races.verdict: An ordinary race at best with only a handful making any serious appeal, MACARONE getting the nod to complete the hat-trick having been value for extra for his recent narrow Bath success. Sub Thirteen looks the obvious threat on paper, while Blue Point Express turned in her best effort of the season at Chepstow last time so she should be on the premises with a repeat.

runners.note: Showed ability in maiden/novices for other yards in 2024. Little impact after a 21-month absence on handicap/stable debut at Chepstow in June but left that behind when third at Leicester the following month. Failed to bu
Three-time winner in 2025 and made the frame twice on all-weather early this year. Disappointed since, though, including on recent return from 4-month absence at Bath.
Fourteen runs since his last win but he arrives in good nick, third of 17 at Bath (5.7f, good to soft) a fortnight ago. Remains on a career-low mark but will probably find a few too good.

Capitalised on a reduced mark to gain a first win for current yard in 6-runner classified event over C&D last month and followed up returned to a handicap in 8-runner event at Bath (5.7f, good to firm) just over 2 weeks
Still a way from bettering poor form and may have found the 1f longer trip stretching her when last seen at Wolverhampton (7f) 10 months ago. Watching brief advised having moved yards since.

Regressive maiden for Richard and Peter Fahey in July and little short-term promise to glean from both starts for new connections, proving to free in first-time blinkers at Southwell (6f) last month. Handicapper drops hi

Maiden who isn't one to be interested in.
Only success came in May 2024 and seemingly retains little ability.
Has shown precious little on all 5 starts, latest after 7 months off on turf debut.
Poor ex-Irish maiden who is yet to offer much in a handful of 6f handicaps for new yard in recent weeks. Easy to look elsewhere.
Has failed to beat a rival all 4 starts this summer, including on handicap debut last time.

races.name: Army Equitation Centenary Irish European Breeders Fund Maiden
races.verdict: HMAS PERTH left his debut form behind when runner-up at Doncaster earlier this month, pulling clear of the rest, and he looks to hold leading claims of getting off the mark this time around. Maximilien Luce boasts a fine pedigree and helps to give Aidan O'Brien a strong hand in the race, with Yellow Sky completing the shortlist.

runners.note: Son of Gleneagles who raced freely before dropping away to finish last of 8 in maiden at Leopardstown (1m) on debut 7 weeks ago. However, yard's juveniles have tended to need their first run this season, so he could leav
Foaled March 17. €15,000 yearling, Saxon Warrior gelding. Dam 1m winner who stayed 1¼m. Faces a difficult task first time up.
Foaled February 9. No Nay Never colt. Half-brother to Canadian 7f winner Tempo Madness. Dam US 1m winner (including at 2 yrs). Worth a market check on debut.

Improved on debut form when second of 10 in maiden at Doncaster (1m) 15 days ago, only narrowly denied by another promising type. Holds a Group 1 entry and he's the one to beat with further progress to come.
Making his first start, ran green when eighth of 11 in maiden at Naas 10 days ago. Likely to need more time.

Foaled February 10. St Mark's Basilica colt. Closely related to 1m winner Always Happy. Dam, 9f winner who stayed 1½m, half-sister to 7f winner Wading and winner up to 1½m Bracelet (both smart). Makes plenty of appeal on
€200,000 breeze-up purchase but shaped as if he would benefit from his first outing when seventh of 18 in maiden at Naas (6f) in July. Could see a better showing this time around.

Foaled March 10. 110,000 gns yearling, €68,000 2-y-o, Mehmas colt. Brother to useful 2-y-o 5f/6f winner Ballistic Missile. Yard not known for winning 2-y-o newcomers.
Foaled March 18. €35,000 yearling, Ghaiyyath colt. Dam maiden (stayed 13.5f) half-sister to useful French 1¼m/11f winner Beau Vengerov. Bred to need further down the line.

Half-brother to 3 winners, including the trainer's multiple Group 1 winner Precise, but looked very much in need of the experience when seventh of 11 in maiden over this C&D on debut last month. Can be expected to know a
Slowly away and always behind on debut when thirteenth of 15 in maiden at Naas 10 days ago. Looks one for the longer term.

Foaled March 20. €16,000 yearling, resold €9,000 yearling, Showcasing colt. Dam unraced half-sister to very smart 5f winner (including Prix de l'Abbaye) Wizz Kid out of useful 6.7f winner Lidanski. Yard's only other 2-y-

Foaled March 26. €47,000 yearling, Lucky Vega colt. Half-brother to several winners, including winner up to 7f Megarry (2-y-o 6f winner) and useful 7f/1m winner Gypsy Woman. Dam maiden (stayed 7f). May just be better for

Shaped encouragingly on debut when 6½ lengths fifth of 8 to next-time-out Group 2 scorer Giant Sequoia in maiden over this C&D in June. Possibly unsuited by the track when well held at the Galway Festival, so he's worth
Foaled May 5. €10,000 yearling, Nando Parrado filly. Closely related to 2-y-o 1m winner Iamimmaculate, and half-sister to 3 winners, including useful 2-y-o 7.4f winner in Italy Azul Bahia.

races.name: Betfred 'Turbo Boost' Nursery
races.verdict: GIVE HAND showed much improved form on his second start when third over C&D, the race won by a promising newcomer, and he could be up to making a successful nursery debut with his yard going well. Regal Tiger has been going the right way in his 3 outings so far and is next on the list, ahead of The Ginger Kid.

runners.note: Off the mark in a Nottingham novice (6f) on second start. Found things tough at Royal Ascot but has been running well in 7f nurseries since, shaping as if still in decent form when sixth of 18 at York's Ebor meeting. Res

Resumed progress when runner-up on nursery debut at Lingfield (6f, good to firm) in August. Didn't need to improve when going one better in 5-runner maiden at Brighton last time, though more required here back in a nurse

Confirmed debut promise when winning a Kempton novice (7f) last month. Failed to see out 1m at the first attempt when sixth of 8 in nursery at Sandown 16 days ago, so he could bounce back returned to this trip.

In need of the experience on debut and stepped forward from that effort when third of 10 in an interesting-looking novice over this C&D 17 days ago. Well-bred type and makes plenty of appeal sent handicapping on only his

Has progressed with each start so far, making a quick switch to nurseries when ½-length second of 6 at Windsor (6f) in July. The winner that day scored next time so he merits consideration with prospect of more to come u

Resumed progress back up to 6f for nursery debut when going close at Nottingham last month, form boosted since. Faced a stiffer task in sales race at Newmarket next outing, but ran poorly back in a nursery at Doncaster (
Showed ability in both starts last month, no extra only late on when third of 8 in maiden over this C&D on latest outing. Makes nursery debut.

Took a step forward on his third run when second of 5 in novice at Brighton in August. However, he wasn't in the same form when down the field in nursery at Newbury last time, unable to get away with racing freely on tha

races.name: Bridge, The Home Of The Carvery Nursery
races.verdict: RHODES RUNNER readily got off the mark in a heavy-ground novice at Chester last time and is fancied to follow up. Knock Three Times could be the main danger if headgear has the desired effect. Perigord Noir, Wolf's Gallop and Naval Cop are also worthy of consideration in a tight nursery.

runners.note: Found improvement faced with heavy ground for the first time at Chester 8 days ago, readily winning a 6f novice in good style. She isn't fully exposed under these conditions and may well follow up back in a nursery.

€50,000 Showcasing colt who ran to a similar level when runner-up in 5f novices at Windsor/Chepstow earlier this month. Now switches to handicap following 10 weeks away and his opening mark demands a bit more.

Improved to make a winning nursery debut at Lingfield (6f, good to firm) in July. Shaped as if back in form when 2¼-length fourth at Bath (5f) last time, when outpaced before running on. First-time cheekpieces/softer gro

Highly tried on the back of her first-time-out success at Thirsk in the spring. Sights lowered and looked ready for return to 5f when 2¾ lengths fourth of 7 in a Redcar seller (6f, 5/1) last time. Will need to bounce bac

Went close on second start in a nursery at Chepstow (5f, soft) last month. Backed that up in change of headgear (still hung right) when 1½-length third in above-average nursery for this grade at Bath latest. Conditions h

Went the right way in maiden/novices, showing plenty of speed when third on qualifying run at Windsor (5f). Beaten less than a length when well-backed fourth on nursery bow at Leicester. Possibly unsuited by surface/shar

Hails from talented sprinting family. Improved a fair bit to make a winning nursery debut at Chepstow (5f, soft). Found life tougher in higher grade when 4½-length third at Chester last time (having been well drawn). Ent
Standout effort when a 50/1 runner-up under similar conditions over C&D on second career start. That was a weak maiden, though, and it's hardly been a positive start in nurseries.

races.name: Izuzu Ireland Irish European Breeders Fund Maiden
races.verdict: Aidan O'Brien looks to have a strong hand in this but not for the first time this season he may have to play second fiddle to son Joseph, CLUSTER selected to go a couple of places better than on debut (yard's juvenile runners tend to come on appreciably from their debut). Kingdom of Camelot is seemingly the choice of Ryan Moore, so he heads up the dangers, with Greatest Knight and Capability Brown

runners.note: Ten Sovereigns colt who shaped as if in need of the experience when last of 15 in maiden at Naas (7f, good to soft) on debut 10 days ago. Up in trip.
Much better effort in maidens at this track when 1¾ lengths third of 10 to Zarak Pasha in C&D event last month. More needed again if he's to be involved.
Showed the benefit of initial experience when third of 15 in maiden at Gowran (7f, good to soft) last month. Upped in trip and can progress again.

Frankel colt who produced a promising first effort when third of 13 in maiden at this course (1m, good to soft) last month. Yard's runners often come on appreciably from their debut so he's one to keep an eye on.
Well held in 2 turf maidens 3 months apart (gelded after debut). Upped markedly in trip.

Zarak colt who looked badly in need of the experience when sixth of 8 in maiden at this course (7f, good to firm) on debut back in June. Upped in trip and no surprise should he leave that bare form behind.

Foaled February 13. Camelot colt. Dam, 1m-9.5f winner, half-sister to smart 1m-9.5f winner (stayed 1½m) White Wolf out of smart winner up to 8.3f (2-y-o 6f/7f winner) Long Lashes. Of obvious interest. Yard 7-62 with 2-y-

€1,200,000 Camelot colt who caught the eye under considerate handling when fourth of 13 in maiden at this course (1m, good to soft) on debut last month, seeming to finish with running left. Appeal as the type to do much
Blue Point colt who went with little encouragement when twelfth of 13 in maiden at this course (1m, good to soft) on debut last month.
Foaled May 14. €50,000 yearling, No Nay Never colt. Half-brother to smart winner up to 1¼m Waliyak. Betting should guide expectations first time up.

Foaled April 7. 70,000 gns yearling, 90,000 gns 2-y-o, Too Darn Hot colt. Brother to 1¼m winner Keble Spirit, and half-brother to 1m winner A E Housman and US winner up to 9.5f Activist Investing. Worth a cursory market
Foaled February 10. 70,000 gns yearling, Space Blues colt. Half-brother to several winners, including smart 1¼m-2m winner Alalcance and useful 1½m-2m winner Achnamara. Likely outsider on debut.

races.name: Betfred Derby 'Wild Card' EBF Conditions Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: Tough to rule out any of the quintet but preference is for ROSE MOON, who looked potentially useful when scoring with something in hand at Salisbury earlier in the month and Ralph Beckett's colt is open to any amount of improvement. Quite Cheeky also made a winning start here recently, so he's put forward as the main threat quickly upped in trip, with Al Wathba rounding off the shortlist.

runners.note: Masar colt who built on debut promise with victory in 8-runner maiden at Lingfield (7f) in May. Caused a 33/1 shock when making all on nursery debut at Glorious Goodwood (7f, good to firm) in July but not good enough upp

Scopey €900,000 Wootton Bassett colt who shaped well when behind the subsequent Acomb winner Haffner on debut. Turned over at 2/11 next start, but made no mistake at Kempton (1m) last month. However, proved too free when

Improved to make a winning start to his nursery career over 7f here last month. Looked a cut above his rivals when following up from 2 lb higher at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) last time and while this demands more, he sh

70,000 gns yearling, Teofilo colt who overcame inexperience to make a winning debut in 10-runner novice at this course (7f, good) earlier in the month, the trio completing the frame all having had a run. Upped in trip an

€95,000 yearling, Sea The Moon colt who knew his job and looked potentially useful in scoring with something in hand in 9-runner novice at Salisbury (1m, good to soft) on debut earlier in the month. Will stay further in

races.name: Bridge, Family Run And Proud Handicap
races.verdict: BAMA LAMA has fallen a long way in the weights and looks potentially interesting with Saffie Osborne taking over. She's narrowly preferred to Some Nightmare, who's been knocking on the door, while Call Time is still potentially well treated under a penalty for last week's win here. In-form Outer Edge looks set to be in the shake-up, too, in a trappy sprint.

runners.note: Seems best on soft/heavy ground. Built on promise of his previous run when seeing off 2 last-time-out winners to score over 6f here (soft) on Monday. Still potentially well-treated under a 5-lb penalty and looks more str

Ground-versatile C&D winner. Has been running well in his bid to snap a losing streak stretching back to last summer, getting within ½-length of in-form Macarone at Bath (6f, good to firm) latest. Capable of running anot

Popped up with a win (off higher marks) in each of the previous 2 years. Finished 1¼ lengths behind next-time-out winner Macarone in a 6f course handicap last month. Backed that up with close fourth in blanket finish at

Quirky C&D winner. Tumbled in weights since last win in October 2024. Friendless in the betting/hasn't fired this season, latterly 6¾ lengths behind Call Time here (6f, soft, 33/1) last Monday. Could be worth a chance in
Lightly-raced 3-y-o who has achieved little at long odds in 6f/7f races to date. Hard to be confident of better dropped to the minimum trip here.

races.name: Qatar Racing And Equestrian Club Renaissance Stakes (Group 3)
races.verdict: POWER BLUE has fallen short at Group 1 level this year but still looked a smart sort when scoring at this track in a Group 2 in July and this looks a good opportunity to add another success down in trip and grade. Big Gossey is so hard to rule out around here given his incredible course record and he'll run well, while Royal Bay Cen needs considering given how impressive she was fresh earlier in t

Won at Fairyhouse in June and produced good second in a listed race here later that month. Proved vulnerable in handicaps last 2 starts and this task may prove beyond him.

In top hands but hasn't hit the heights his juvenile campaign promised and looked laboured when seventh of 17 in a Group 1 over 5f at this course 14 days ago. Back up in trip now and needs a lot more, though did win his

High-class juvenile who won the Norfolk Stakes before missing the rest of his 2-y-o campaign. Returned in April with a routine win in a listed race at Navan but has gone the wrong way since and has plenty of questions to
Useful sort who made frame in listed company over this trip last 2 starts, including when third to Soul Love last time. Also a C&D winner but this demands a lot more.

Ex-French filly who went especially well fresh when winning a listed race impressively on stable debut at Cork on heavy going in May before respectable fourth of 8 in a Group 3 at Naas later that month. Now returns after
British raider who has made up into a useful sprinter with 4 wins from 7 starts and ran well when second of 8 in Group 3 at Naas 35 days ago. Consistent sort who looks sure to give her running.

races.name: Hunt Family Fund Novice Stakes (Sponsored By Betfred) (GBB Race)
races.verdict: BLUE NOON has proved consistent in defeat in handicaps in recent months, not beaten at all far when fifth over this trip at Goodwood 4 weeks ago. She looks to hold sound claims back in novice company with a tongue strap now added. Maestro Del Mar also enters calculations despite conceding weight all round. Seacole and newcomer Rowlf also require a second look.

runners.note: Fairly useful colt who cemented his promising start for new yard when finishing a good second on handicap debut at Kempton (1½m) in August. Found life tougher back in novice grade against 3-y-os when fourth at Southwell
Rerouted gelding. Dam maiden (stayed 8.5f). Yard wouldn't be a known source of winning newcomers in this sphere.

Golden Horn gelding. Half-brother to 1¼m winner Kissmehoneyhoney. Dam, 1½m winner who stayed 2½m, also won in bumpers/over hurdles. Certainly not lacking for stamina judged on pedigree and he's one to note in the betting

Still looking for a breakthrough success but has been running well in handicaps, matching her previous best when finishing close-up fifth at Goodwood (1¼m, good) 30 days ago. Rates a likely player back in novice company.
Raven's Pass filly who has offered little in pair of novice/maiden events in recent weeks.

Fair filly who ran up to her previous best with first-time cheekpieces enlisted (retained) when third of 7 in maiden at Windsor (11.5f) 13 days ago. Not progressing at present but a repeat gives her claims nevertheless.

races.name: Happy Birthday Alex, From The Bridge Handicap
races.verdict: QUEENIE ST CLAIR is potentially very well treated from a mark of 60 back in this sphere given her exploits over hurdles for Nick Schofield last winter and she could well be worthy of siding with having gone well fresh previously. Carthusian proved yet another good advert for the Jennie Candlish team when making a successful yard debut at Chester 8 days ago and rates next best. No Ordinary Joe is o

races.name: Celebrating County Kildare And Lexington Twinning Maiden
races.verdict: Standard-setter VALENTINO ECLIPSE should appreciate this drop to sprinting and comfortably gets the vote. Otsana has had her debut form franked and can go close again, with Lilli's Angel another to consider for each-way purposes.

runners.note: €23,000 yearling, Raven's Pass gelding. Always behind on belated debut at Cork earlier this month and makes little appeal. Hood's left off and the tongue strap goes on.
Calyx gelding. 33/1, caught the eye when sixth of 24 in maiden over C&D (heavy) on debut in April, faring best of those held up. Absent since but looks sure to improve on that.
Third over a similar trip at Naas in minor event on return last month but has gone backwards since. Blinkers go on and holds place claims if the return to 6f sparks a revival.
Starman gelding. Fourteenth of 16 in maiden at Cork (6f, good to soft, 80/1) on debut 28 days ago.

Neck second at Leopardstown on debut in May and took step forward when 2¼ lengths fourth of 13 behind the progressive Loughrea in maiden here (1m, good to firm) when last seen the following month. Sets the bar pretty hig
66/1, very green when last of 15 in maiden at Cork (6f, good to firm) on debut in July 2024. Hooded and can only be watched on first start since.
Lightly-raced filly who's run to a modest level on each start. Needs significant improvement to feature back in a maiden.
Twice-raced filly. Showed more than on debut when seventh of 12 in maiden (66/1) at Down Royal (5f, good) 23 days ago. Needs this run for a mark.
Steadily progressive form in 3 maidens, making the frame at Cork last time. Place claims at best.

Showed ability when fifth on debut at the Curragh and matched that level when third in maiden at Down Royal (5f, good) 23 days ago. Tongue strap goes on. Her form is working out well and she's entitled to be in the mix.
Showed fair ability in maidens prior to shaping as though amiss on handicap bow at Killarney (1m) last month. Has her work cut out, even if back on song.

Australia filly. Sister to 2-y-o 7f winner Expensive Rose and closely related to 8.6f-12.4f winner Flying Scotsman and useful 1½m-17f winner Comfort Zone. Bred more for stamina than speed, may need more time and distance
Made a promising start when third in maiden at Limerick in June, finishing well under hand riding. Was disappointing at Gowran earlier this month and may be one for handicaps.
25/1, tenth of 14 in maiden at Gowran (7f, good to soft) on debut 26 days ago. Probably one for later on.

races.name: Betfred 'Nifty 50' Jump Jockeys Derby Handicap (Professional Jump Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: FOX AVATAR hasn’t yet been able to add to last year’s pair of wins, but is now down to a good mark and, with the step back up in trip expected to suit, he looks worth siding with in an open affair. Completed a quick-fire hat-trick in 4-runner event at Yarmouth in May. Has largely struggled since, though, and has been well beaten on both his previous tries at this trip.

Continues to get better with age, winning twice at Chester this year, posting a career best when landing 11-runner event there 15 days ago by 1¼ lengths from Arrange. Up another 3 lb but looks sure to be involved.

Showed fairly useful form up to 1½m on the Flat in France for Henri-Alex Pantall before being bought by current connections for €38,000. Has shown fair form over hurdles, winning maiden at Plumpton in April. Not seen sin

Winner on the Flat at Newbury last spring. Performed with credit when 6¾ lengths fourth of 9 to King Of Berkshire at Windsor on return from 6-month absence, but this looks tougher.

Successful 3 times this season, with latest win at Leicester in June. Has largely held form since, but got stuck in the heavy ground at Goodwood last time. Now below last winning mark, she's capable of being involved if

races.name: Celebrate In Style At The Bridge Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: SILENT FORCE made a promising start when third in a Newbury novice, beaten only by a pair with the benefit of previous experience, and he can build on that effort to open his account. Ghost Raider is feared most.

runners.note: Bred for further and was never on terms making his first start when ninth of 10 in novice at Epsom (7f) 17 days ago. Looks one for the longer term.
Has shaped encouragingly when making the frame both starts so far, still looking in need of the experience when fourth of 11 in maiden at York 3 weeks ago. Remains capable of better.

Foaled May 2. €60,000 2-y-o, Naval Crown colt. Half-brother to 3 winners, including useful French 2-y-o 5f winner Graft and 2-y-o 6f winner Rishes Baar. Has a fairly useful standard to aim at on debut.
NON RUNNER.
Made plenty of appeal on paper and shaped promisingly amidst greenness when third of 13 in novice at Newbury on debut 6 weeks ago, form boosted since. Major player with improvement to come.

races.name: Darley Fillies Stakes (Group 3)
races.verdict: CURRACLOE looked a very useful prospect when making a winning debut at Gowran and, open to plenty of progress, is taken to make an immediate impact at stakes level. Damsel In Distress was placed at this level last time despite looking stretched by 1m and rates the main danger back at 7f, while Alpine Wedding is respected after improving last time but would be better suited by stepping up to 1m.

races.name: Betfred 'Bet Builder' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: It's hard not to be taken by the potential shown by MATINS and the 3-y-o can maintain the unbeaten start to his career at the expense of the in-form Echalar.

runners.note: Created a fine impression on belated debut when winning 4-runner maiden at Salisbury by 7 lengths from a next-time-out winner in July and effortlessly followed up in a match at Yarmouth last month. Should improve now han
Has disappointed since finishing second in a listed race on the all-weather at Lingfield early last year.  Bled last time. Very hard to make a case for at present.
Fifteen runs since last win in 2025. In first-time visor, fourth of 11 in handicap at Kempton (7f, 7/2) last time. The headgear is dicarded and goes beyond 1m for the first time.

Ran out a ready winner from his easing mark at Doncaster in August, finally proving fully effective at this trip. Backed that up when ½-length second of 7 to Hamlet's Night at Yarmouth (1¼m, good) 12 days ago despite con
Goes well round here and landed a second C&D success earlier in the month having edged below last winning mark. Cheekpieces are now added and can give another good account.

races.name: Bridge, For All Family Occasions Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: ROSEMARY’S ROSE disappointed last time and has proved expensive to follow this season, but she has already run well twice at this course this year and is worth another chance back in 0-60 company. Prince Ali arrives in good form and rates the main threat despite a 6 lb rise, while Homeland can also be involved if putting his best foot forward.

runners.note: Dual 1m all-weather winner over the winter. Has largely been running well whilst proving expensive to follow of late, 1½ lengths third of 8 to Kaleidoscope Eyes in handicap (evens) at this track (7.5f) last month, but th

Dual winner at Chepstow this year, landing a 9-runner 0-55 handicap in June and a 7f similar event there in August, beating Escape Magic by 2¾ lengths on latest. Up 6 lb and now back at 1m, but looks sure to give another
A fair 7f scorer (albeit not straightforward) for Hugo Palmer who signed off for that yard with a good third at Wetherby in June. Not in same form on either start for this stable, though.

Underlined good start for new yard by justifying support to when winning 1¼m handicap at this course in July. Undone by 3 lb rise at Lingfield next time, though, and ran about as well as could be expected from 5 lb out o

Won at Chepstow in June and has pretty much held his form since, though a recent third in a 0-85 event back at Chepstow from 13 lb out of the handicap leaves him on a mark 9 lb above his last winning one.

Wootton Bassett filly who showed plenty to work on when third of 5 in novice at Lingfield (7.5f, good) back in May. Has gone wrong way both stats since and a leap of faith required to make a case for her making an immedi

Maiden who failed to progress for Andrew Balding. Hasn't managed to get seriously competitive for new yard either, though ran one of this season's better races when 2¼ lengths fourth of 8 to Tronido at Epsom last month.
Got off the mark in first-time cheekpieces in 11-runner handicap at Chepstow (7f, soft) last month, suited by being held up in a strongly-run race. Failed to back that up at Bath last time, though.
Unreliable sort. Below-par eighth of 12 in handicap at Wolverhampton (8.6f) 32 days ago, looking a hard ride. Others more persuasive.
Long-standing maiden who has tended to save his best for Newcastle but ran one of his better races when 3 lengths third of 9 to Equion at this course on latest.

races.name: Friends Of The Curragh Irish Cesarewitch (0-110) (Premier Handicap)
races.verdict: An ultra-competitive renewal of this valuable handicap and it may well go the way of Willie Mullins' THE REVEREND. Aidan O'Brien has enjoyed recent success in this race with 3-y-os and his Port Of Spain has to enter calculations. Blake looks a fascinating contender back on the Flat, while Tim Toe, Truth Be Told, Kingstonian and Sky Captain also appeal.

runners.note: Won a listed event and C&D Group 3 here either side of finishing ½-length second in 2025 renewal of this race. Seemingly retains all that ability judged on a couple of starts in 1½m listed races in June, though is 5 lb h

Admirable dual-purpose performer who finished eighth in the Melbourne Cup when last seen on the Flat. Subsequent 3 runs over hurdles were miles from his best (possibly feeling the effects of his globetrotting). Feasibly

Smart Group 2 winner over 15f in France last year. Again flying too high when well beaten in first-time cheekpieces in Irish St Leger here latest. Hard to rule out a revival on return to calmer waters, especially if the

Borderline smart performer who hit the frame in the Ascot Stakes/Chester Cup last season. Finished third in an Irish St Leger Trial prior to running as well as could be expected when well-held fifth in the main event her

Ground-versatile stayer. Things fell right when landing Chester Cup in May. Didn't last out the marathon distance under a typically positive ride in Queen Alexandra at Royal Ascot subsequently. Should fare better back do

Progressive handicapper for William Haggas last autumn. Showed bundles of potential in a couple of hurdle starts prior to running a cracker when 1-length fourth in a Premier Handicap at Leopardstown on return. In excelle

Hasn't stood much racing since his victory in 2024 Queen Alexandra at Ascot. Didn't build on the promise of his comeback run at Galway (1¾m) last time. Will likely need to be back to his very best to defy his mark in a r

Lightly raced in this sphere. Back on the up when runner-up in a 2m Premier Handicap at Galway Festival (arguably unlucky not to win). Still looked unexposed as a stayer prior to trailing the field at Chester 2 weeks ago

Finished well when 7½ lengths behind his stablemate in this corresponding event 12 months ago. Ran well when beaten 2 lengths in a very condensed finish at Leopardstown (13f, good to firm) latest. Tried in another change

Sole British raider. Completed a double in stylish fashion on return at Hamilton (13f). Better than he could show when sixth in Copper Horse at Royal Ascot (1¾m) and again asked to come from a long way back when a non-st

Useful dual-purpose performer. Personal best when third in the Cesarewitch at Newmarket last autumn. Hadn't been pulling up any trees over hurdles prior to never threatening in the Ascot stakes. Makes only second Flat st

Smooth traveller who posted a career-best Flat success at Leopardstown (1½m) on second start for present yard last autumn. Ended novice hurdle season with cracking second Grade 1 Champion Novice at Punchestown in April.

Bred for jumps but has proved remarkably versatile regards ground trip. Added to his bumper/1½m maiden wins when successful in a 1m conditions event at Listowel in May. Travelled as well as any when well-backed third ove

Fairly useful hurdle winner (2m, heavy). Runner-up in top-end handicap at Galway before gamely going one better in a similar event at Leopardstown (13f). No easy task to defy a 7-lb penalty in a race this competitive and

Low-mileage 5-y-o. Winner of a Roscommon maiden (1½m) on debut last summer. Useful form to finish runner-up on each of his 3 subsequent outings for Paddy Twomey. Shaped well returning over much shorter when sixth on stab

Smart hurdler. Much-improved fourth behind Comfort Zone in 2m Premier Handicap at Galway Festival on penultimate start. No obvious excuses for his subsequent disappointment at Killarney, for all he's still relatively ear

Sole Flat success came in a Leopardstown maiden in 2024. Has acquitted herself with plenty of credit in ultra-competitive staying handicaps this season. Arrives on the back of a creditable 2-length third in 1½ listed eve

Hasn't entirely proved his stamina in a handful of starts over staying trips, latterly when eighth behind stable Comfort Zone at Galway. Now back up in trip sporting more headgear, having not been disgraced in 13f handic

Forward-going handicapper who's been admirably consistent despite not winning for over 2 years. As good as ever when 1-length second at Chester (2m) last time. Likely needs to improve for the addition of cheekpieces, if

Useful juvenile who's developed into a smart performer this year. Suited by well-run race when narrowly denied in handicap at Naas (11f). Certainly bred for longer trips (half-brother to Park Hill winner) and very intere

2025 Fred Winter winner who was successful in the 2025 renewal of this race off 9 lb lower mark. Had excuses for several starts across both codes since, though ran no sort of race without obvious reason in Galway Hurdle

Useful 4-y-o handicapper who's improved for current connections this year. Caught further back than ideal when beaten 2 lengths in a very valuable handicap at Leopardstown (13f). Has stamina on his dam's side and interes

Smooth-travelling mare who's been lightly raced since 2024. Looked as good as ever when successful in Amateur Riders Derby here (1½m) last October. Didn't get the gaps on return at Galway (2m) and type who'll be ridden t

Useful for Christophe Ferland in France in 2024. Hasn't stood much racing recently, hitting the frame in couple of maiden hurdles and probably needing her comeback (10.5f) at Sligo last month. On handy mark if recapturin

Chester Plate runner-up who improved when 2 lengths fourth in valuable Galway handicap in July. Returns to Flat in first-time visor following promising third on hurdling debut last month. Potentially well treated and sti

Low-mileage 5-y-o who returned with a cosy win at Gowran. Back on the up when runner-up in a useful handicap at Killarney (14.5f). Could well be more to come with cheekpieces added back up in trip, and looks one of the s

Hasn't matched the pick of his useful juvenile form in trio starts this season. Did at least run a bit better when beaten 4¾ lengths on handicap bow at Down Royal (13f, soft) in June. Another unexposed Joseph O'Brien run

Flat maiden who shaped well when sixth in the 2024 renewal of this race. Hasn't been at the peak of his powers in 3 starts on the Flat this year, however, he's dropped to a reasonable mark for a yard more than capable of

Successful in 2m Clonmel handicap on latest Flat start this time last year. Reverts to the level on the back of a breakthrough success in a mares maiden hurdle at Downpatrick latest. Another who needs a career best.

This race mooted as a target following a second success of the year at Galway in July. Finished 6 lengths off Highwayman prior to finishing well beaten at Leopardstown (13f, 25/1) last time. At least worth noting for eac

Shaped well when sixth to Comfort Zone in 2m Galway handicap in July. Again ran well when close third to Immutable at Leopardstown (13f) latest. Contrasting conditions will hold no fears and while weighted to be competit
Back down to the mark he landed the Cesarewitch from in 2024. Hasn't won since but not disgraced when beaten 10½ lengths at Goodwood (2½m) latest. Considered, especially if supported RESERVE.
Dual Flat winner in France for Francis-Henri Graffard. Didn't offer much on return/first Flat start for present yard earlier this month. Needs a fair bit more here. RESERVE

races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap
races.verdict: CROWN OFFICE is well treated on his best form and looks likely to make a bold bid from an inside draw. He's preferred to fast-improving Thanos and C&D winner Swiped.

runners.note: Mohaather gelding. Won twice over 6f in useful juvenile season. Hasn't gone on from his near miss in this grade at Goodwood in June. First-time cheekpieces could help remedy recent slow starts. Step up in trip/booking of

Successful in change of headgear over C&D prior to improving/following up in more fluent fashion at Sandown later in July. Clearly didn't give his running when bidding for a hat-trick at Ripon (possibly amiss) since. Lea

Dual all-weather winner who ran up to his best well-backed second at Sandown on penultimate start. Testing conditions possibly a factor in his subsequent below-par effort at Haydock. No excuses on that front here and che

Strong-travelling/ground-versatile 3-y-o. Successful on 3 of his last 4 starts, forging clear to win on first start in open company at Chepstow (1m, soft) last time. Faces better opposition here, however, a 7-lb rise may

Consistent sort who gained a deserved first win for his current yard in a Class 5 handicap at Sandown (1m). Form of his subsequent 3½-length third at Windsor has taken a few knocks. May fall short in a better race here,

Landed the odds in a solid 6f Leicester maiden (soft) on final juvenile outing. Best effort since when second to an improving filly at Nottingham (1¼m) prior to disappointing back down in trip at Haydock latest. Still we

Fair maiden for George Boughey. Built on first run for current connections when fairly useful winner over C&D handicap latest. She did have a good pitch in a messy race on that occasion, though, and needs more again up i

Completed a double in a 7f course handicap for Marco Botti last year. Changed hands for 34,000 gns and had been gelded prior to an underwhelming stable debut here earlier this month (hung left). Has a bit to prove back o

Typically ridden patiently when doubling his tally for the year at this course (7f) last month. Still in good heart when 5½ lengths third over C&D last time. Probably needs a strong pace to hold his own back up in grade

races.name: Bridge, For All Family Occasions Handicap (Div 2)
races.verdict: ARVANA BELLE has been runner-up twice at this course in the last month and looked unlucky not to win just 6 days ago, going with zest but unable to fully open up until angled into the clear. She can go one better. Kaleidoscope Eyes has won twice here and could be a threat if suited by the step back up to 1m, whilst Desiderata is looking more reliable of late.

runners.note: Won over 7f here in August for her second course success and ran well when second of 8 over same trip at Chepstow on soft going 29 days ago. Not had much racing at 1m but ground conditions will suit her here so could go
Off the mark at Lingfield for Jack Jones in January but not so good since and ran badly when down field at Bath in July on second outing for current yard. Absent since and is hard to fancy.

On long losing run and raced mainly at longer trips than this in 2026 but in reasonable form before blip at Bath earlier in the month. Handles ground conditions so not without hope down at this level.
Won a claimer in March at Dundalk on all-weather but little promise on turf either start since joining this yard.

Won first handicap at Nottingham over 1m in April, then ran creditably when fifth of 12 in 9f contest at Wolverhampton in August after 4 months off. Has shown quirks in the past but seems more reliable right now and coul
Ended losing run when won C&D handicap 6 days ago, all out to hold on by a short-head. More required turned out quickly under a penalty.
Best effort to date when fourth of 11 in a handicap at Yarmouth 28 days ago, keeping on and looking well worth a try at this trip. Less exposed than most of these so needs considering.

Off the mark at Chepstow over 6f in June but has an inconsistent profile. Creditable second of 11 in handicap over 7f at same track 27 days ago but needs to prove herself as well suited by this step back up to 1m on soft

Off the mark at Bath in June and ran well to be second of 14 there on good to firm going 15 days ago but hung right and carried head awkwardly when hitting the front. That head carriage is a concern as is today's likely

Runner-up twice at this course in last 3 starts, including when going with zest on soft ground when second of 9 6 days ago, looking a shade unlucky not to collect having had to wait for a run. Evidently well suited by co

races.name: Kwiff More Bang For Your Bet Nursery Handicap
races.verdict: MOON SAND has shaped as if handicapping will be his bag and it would be no surprise should he step up markedly now switched to nurseries. Romance has been running well of late and can continue in form, with Gabby Hayes and Closefield Beau heading the list of dangers of the rest.

runners.note: Showed plenty to work on first time up when second in maiden at Roscommon (7.5f) in May. Unsuited by the drop back to 6f in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot next start but has disappointed both starts since. Needs a ret

Went off big prices in 3 maidens and duly shaped as if being brought along with handicaps in mind. Remains open to improvement and is worth noting should the market speak in his favour now switched to nurseries.

Improved effort with a tongue tie added when winning 10-runner event on nursery debut at Down Royal at the beginning of this month. Backed up that effort when runner-up at Listowel 5 days ago. Can go well again.
Close third at Leopardstown second time up, splitting a now-useful Ballydoyle pair, but hasn't come close to reproducing that since. Hard to make a case for at present.
Thrice-raced maiden who's been brought along steadily. Interesting with Keane in the saddle and betting probably best guide now handicapping.
No better than mid-division in 3 maidens, catching the eye at Gowran last month with a view to taking this step into nurseries. One to note in the market.
Finished in mid-field on last 2 of 3 starts in maidens, not given a hard time of things. May do better now handicapping.

Free-going filly who was much improved to open her account in 6-runner nursery over C&D (good to soft, 9/1) last time by ½-length from Luca Brillante from 6 lb out of the weights. Needs more to follow up.

Ran to a modest level in maidens whilst catching the eye with a view to handicapping, though failed to improve switched to nurseries at Fairyhouse last week, merely closing up late. Will appreciate the return to this lon

With the headgear discarded, 10/1, much improved second of 13 in nursery at Naas (1m, good to soft) 10 days ago, nearest finish. Big danger if repeating that but it's a concern that the cheekpieces are quickly refitted.
Gelded and showed a bit more than previously when eighth of 13 on nursery debut at Naas (1m, good to soft) 10 days ago. However, he looks to be on a stiff mark and headgear is now added.
Has looked limited in 3 starts to date and is hard to make a case for from 8 lb out of the weights on handicap bow.

races.name: Betfred 'Follow Us On X' Handicap
races.verdict: MUSICAL ANGEL won this race from a similar mark last year and a recent second over C&D served warning that she's ready to strike again. Velvet Rhythm shaped really well last time and is very much respected but her blowout on sole start at this track is a concern, while Silver Trumpet could go well if starting better than last time.

runners.note: Won this race from 1 lb higher mark last year when with Andrew Balding and ran her best race since when second of 9 over C&D 17 days ago. Looks sure to go well.
Creditable efforts back to back at Kempton on all-weather with hood and cheekpieces, finishing fifth of 9 32 days ago. Down slightly in grade here but not so consistent on turf.

Better known for 6f exploits, finishing a good third of 26 at Goodwood in July, but he's not proving so good at this trip and was last on soft going earlier this month. Visor replaces blinkers but looks best opposed.
Twice a C&D winner, including in July, but not good at the start when fifth of 9 over C&D 17 days ago. Capable of making a big impact if breaking on terms in first-time blinkers.

Won 4 times on turf earlier in the year and shaped very well when third of 12 at Wolverhampton on all-weather 9 days ago, keeping on well having started awkwardly. Ran poorly on sole start at this track in August but hol

Better effort when third of 8 in a 5f handicap at Sandown in August but unseated when jinking in first-time cheekpieces 16 days ago. Cheekpieces removed and he needs to prove himself as well suited by this step back up t

Yet to win on turf but finished runner-up 3 times in a row in handicaps before seventh of 11 over 1m at Ascot 23 days ago, turned out quickly and doing too much too soon. Back down in trip here but not sure to get her wa
Yet to fire since joining current connections, including when fifth of 6 over C&D in a handicap 27 days ago when took strong hold and weakened. Hard to fancy in current form.

Scored at 33/1 when off the mark at Windsor over 6f in May on handicap debut but has since pulled up there and finished ninth of 11 at Kempton in July. Now tries first-time visor and steps back up to 7f after 87 days off
5f winner on all-weather in December but no progress this year. Possibly needed run when eighth of 13 in a handicap at Yarmouth 10 days ago on return from a 3-month break.

races.name: Bridge Llangennech Open Daily Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
races.verdict: By no means a deep handicap so a repeat of the level WELLWHATSHAPPENIN achieved when runner-up in a 1m handicap here a week ago may well suffice. Georg Zhukov was tight in the betting when behind the selection in that aforementioned race and he can be a factor, while The Ormer Gatherer may well show more this time.

runners.note: Signed off 2025 in good form but ended time for Eddie & Patrick Harty on a low-key note. Tongue tied on second start for this yard and right back on his game when runner-up in a 1m course handicap last week. Back up in t

Off the mark over 1m at Dundalk in January. Went into his shell after for Eamonn O'Connell and having been well backed, he didn't revive on stable debut when fourth over 1m here last week (behind Wellwhatshappenin). Back

First form for current yard when second of 10 in all-weather classified event at Lingfield (1½m) last month. Wasn't in same form under a more forceful ride at Wolverhampton since and now back in handicap company dropped

Caused 66/1 shock over 1m at Southwell in January. Went as close as she has since in classified event at Lingfield last month and still in form when 1½-length fourth over longer trip there (1½m) next time. Never able to

Rejoined Mrs A. Malzard when landing handicap at Les Landes (1¼m, good to firm) in June 2025. Big price and almost certainly needed the run for another new yard after 15 months off 2 weeks ago. This will reveal more.
Placed twice in handicaps over this trip at the start of the summer. A trio of lesser efforts have followed, though and a hood is now left off.

races.name: Kwiff Supercharged Betting (Q.R.) Handicap
races.verdict: CHIPSRDOWN has been a different proposition since fitted with a visor and with this step up in trip expected to suit, she can defy the handicapper again. Bhean Saibhre has a lowly mark to exploit and is a huge threat if lining up here, with It's Good To Talk a potential improver.

runners.note: Hurdles winner but she arrives on a lengthy losing run and opening mark in this code looks high on balance of her form this summer.

Went without headgear and bounced back to best when second of 18 at Cork (1½m, good to soft) 4 weeks ago. First-time tongue tied applied and wouldn't be sure to be in the same mood given overall profile.

Largely running well without winning this season, most recently when fifth of 14 at Punchestown (1m, good) 12 days ago. Back up in trip with usual cheekpieces returned and he can make his presence felt.
Matched his peak form when winning 15-runner handicap at this course (12f, soft) in October. Not in the same form over C&D 17 days later and off the track since, so he's entitled to need this.

Has responded really well to the application of a visor, bagging her first win at Leopardstown in June and improving another chunk when driven clear to follow up at Gowran last week. Up 8 lb but she's thriving and this s
Well held in a bumper and no real encouragement to glean from 3 starts in maidens/handicap debut this summer. Yard in good order and blinkers may sharpen him up.
Fair form in bumpers but well held in 4 Flat maidens. Handicaps more suitable though and he needs a market check given the yard he represents.
Winner in France who struggled from an inflated mark in the spring for Denis Hogan. Made more of an impact in claiming company and a tongue strap goes on starting out for new connections.

Proving expensive to follow for current yard, runner-up 3 times this summer. Not at that level the last twice, albeit he was held up in a steadily-run race 3 weeks ago. Step back up in trip should help his cause.
Dropped a fair way in the weights since last spring and she finally cashed in at Roscommon 40 days ago on second start for this yard. Back up 6 lb but she can be a factor again.

Hails from a quality Aga Khan family. Shaped well when close third of 13 in 1m handicap at the Curragh (good) last month. Not in the same form on softer ground at Cork since but might be worth another chance trying this

Bounced back to best when winning 1½m claimer at Tramore in July and good second in a similar race at Killarney (1m, good) next time. Unable to continue the good work at Sligo and more on her plate back in a handicap.

Won twice in summer of 2025 fitted with cheekpieces. Just denied at Leopardstown in May and best effort since when third over hurdles at Wexford 6 weeks ago. Capable of getting involved from this sort of mark.
Made all in better company at Roscommon (1½m) last May. Ran better than for a while when fifth over the same C&D last month but taken on for the lead and was brushed aside at Cork 4 weeks ago.
Tongue strap on for first time when a resurgent fourth of 6 in handicap at Limerick (12.5f) in July but failed badly to back that up dropped to 1m here last month.
Runner-up in maiden company on all-weather in July but mid-field both efforts on turf since. Blinkers need to galvanise her.

All-weather winner in November and with headgear on for the first time, he left previous effort this season behind when second of 4 in handicap at Newmarket (1¼m, good) 43 days ago. Cheekpieces now applied and he's unexp
Looked a work-in-progress in her qualifying runs and appeals as the type to raise her game now handicapping.
Low-key reappearance/handicap debut but much more like it when fourth over 8.5f at Galway in July. Latest effort easy to excuse having been snatched up.
Showed much more than previously when eighth in a big-field maiden at Navan 3 weeks ago, never nearer. Opening mark very fair on that evidence.
Minor promise only for Jack W. Davison last summer. Gelded ahead of stable/handicap debut and didn't show much in March. Off again since.
Career-best success over hurdles at Kilbeggan (19f) last month and ran respectably back on the level at Dundalk on Friday. One to consider if turning out again quickly.
Retains little ability these days.
Right back on her game when fourth over hurdles at Galway in July. Wasn't on her game back on the level 2 weeks later but given a short break since.
